summary: Implementation is clean and well-structured. The three key concerns are: (1) hash inconsistency risk between lookup and storage keys, (2) empty-content guard missing in signMemory(), (3) VerifyMemoryOutput type intersection is semantically loose.

findings.title: Idempotency lookup uses SHA-256 but INSERT may store server's blake3 hash
findings.description: contentHashOf() produces a SHA-256 hex. The idempotency SELECT uses this SHA-256 hash. But the INSERT on line 113 stores signResult.contentHash (server blake3) when present. On a second call for the same content, the SELECT will look up the SHA-256 hash but the row was stored with the blake3 hash — the idempotency check will miss and you'll re-sign.
findings.recommendation: Always use SHA-256 as the dedup key in both the SELECT and the INSERT. Store the server's blake3 hash in a separate column (e.g. server_content_hash) for auditing if needed, but keep content_hash as the canonical SHA-256 lookup key throughout.

findings.title: No empty-content guard before signing
findings.description: MnemonicClient.signMemory() throws UserError for empty content (seen in client.ts line 162). signMemory() in sign.ts does not validate content before passing it to adapter.sign(). This means the UserError surfaces as a generic 'Mnemonik signing failed' message rather than a clear 'content must not be empty' message.
findings.recommendation: Add an early guard: `if (!content || !content.trim()) return { error: 'content must not be empty' };`

findings.title: VerifyMemoryOutput uses intersection type but VerifyResult is a discriminated union
findings.description: `VerifyResult & { error?: string }` creates a type that TypeScript cannot narrow correctly — narrowing on `status` won't correctly exclude the `error` field. The cast `as VerifyMemoryOutput` on lines 40, 43, 47 suppresses the real type mismatch.
findings.recommendation: Define VerifyMemoryOutput as a union: `type VerifyMemoryOutput = VerifyResult | { status: 'not_found'; error: string };` or wrap the result: `return { ...result };`
findings.note: Low practical impact since callers check `result.error` first, but worth fixing for correctness.

findings.title: createMnemonikAdapter overrides parameter has all-optional fields with no type guard
findings.description: The overrides object allows an empty `{}` call. The function body then falls back to env vars for all fields. This is fine but the type `{ jwt?: string; ... }` parameter combined with the default `= {}` means TypeScript infers `jwt` as `string | undefined` — calling code cannot rely on the compiler to catch missing required fields.
findings.recommendation: Document explicitly that this is intentional (env-var-first) or split into separate required/optional params. Current implementation is correct, just document the intent.
